claim: The Philippine Competition Commission found that six onion importers, traders, a freight forwarder and a cold-storage firm divided up the onion trade, and fined them a combined ₱1.76 billion, the largest fine under the Competition Act.
status: Ruling; most of the firms have asked the PCC to reconsider, so the fines are not yet final

claim: The National Bureau of Investigation filed a complaint against six people for hoarding and profiteering in onion sales in December 2022.
A House committee said in May 2023 that an onion cartel was allegedly operating, and that the late-2022 price rise was not justified by the shortage.
status: Committee finding; not a court ruling

claim: In December 2024, House lawmakers alleged that rice importers and traders colluded to keep prices high after the tariff cut, with one saying they gained about ₱13 billion.
status: Alleged at a House hearing; no charges reported

suspect: Spoilage on the way to market
claim: A 2019 study of Benguet farmers says about 42% of Philippine vegetable harvests are wasted to spoilage.
source_name: Journal of Environmental Science and Management (UPLB)
